title: Exact approaches for convex adjustable robust optimization
headline: Open finding: Theorem 2’s equivalence result survives, but its convex MINLP classification fails for an allowed negative uncertainty set.

work.title: Exact approaches for convex adjustable robust optimization

claims.label: Theorem 2 convex-MINLP classification
claims.gist: Theorem 2 adds that formulation (8) is a convex MINLP whenever X is a convex MINLP set, without requiring nonnegative uncertainty.
claims.statement: Under Assumptions 1–2, Theorem 2 states an equivalence and classifies formulation (8) as a convex MINLP whenever X is a convex MINLP set. The equivalence conclusion is supported; the classification fails under the assumptions as written.
conditions: Assumption 1 requires the stated real-valued convex data functions.
Assumption 2 requires the stated Z-sets to be closed; Lemma 1 supplies it for the compact nonempty recourse sets in the witness.
The theorem does not require Xi to be componentwise nonnegative.
claims.quantifiers: Under Assumptions 1–2, for every permitted convex-MINLP first-stage set X and uncertainty set Xi, formulation (8) is claimed to be a convex MINLP; the witness uses Xi={−1}.

result.summary: A compact-recourse instance with Xi={-1} yields a nonconvex epigraph and a nonconvex semi-infinite cut under the stated assumptions; the equivalence conclusion survives.
result.witness: Take X=[-1,1], Xi={-1}, f11(x)=x^2, g1(x,y)=y^2+1, and g0(x,y)=0. These functions are real-valued and convex. The recourse set is empty for |x|<1 and {0} at x=±1, so every nonempty recourse set is compact and the required closedness holds. For an admissible cut with lambda0=lambda1=alpha>0, the paper's sigma is alpha(1-x^2-x0). The cut contains (0,-1) and (0,1) but excludes their midpoint (0,0).
result.argument: A convex MINLP feasible region must be convex in its continuous relaxation. The displayed cut is nonconvex, and the robust epigraph is {(x0,x): x0>=0, x in {-1,1}}, also nonconvex. Thus the classification fails under an allowed signed uncertainty set, while the separate equivalence statement remains supported.
not_claimed: The note does not challenge applications with nonnegative uncertainty or later fixed-x separation results.
No defect is claimed when an appropriate sign-compatibility condition is imposed.
result.repair_note: A nonnegative uncertainty set or another sign-compatibility condition may repair the convexity argument; the equivalence result is separate.
